summary: 90s-2010s nostalgia toys + virtual-pet plushies + vintage TCG + iconic franchise pieces with sustained collector resale. Millennial buyers (now 28-44 with disposable income) are buying back their childhoods — items that mass-market resellers dismiss as 'kid junk' often have surprisingly strong floors. Sweet spot: $20-150 typical, $200+ on sealed-tag Webkinz / unused codes / Pokemon 1st Ed / Polly Pocket Bluebird / vintage Cabbage Patch Coleco. STRICT focus on small-box / poly-mailer ship class — skips full doll cases / large playsets / oversized plush. The matcher uses era markers (Bluebird, Pleasant Company, Coleco, McDonald's Happy Meal vintage) to disambiguate vintage premium tier from modern commodity reissues.
field_workflow: Webkinz: hangtag MUST be attached + UNCUT — clipped tags drop value 80%. The unused secret code (visible through plastic on tag) is what trades; cut tags = $5 commodity
Neopets: McDonald's Happy Meal 2004-2006 promo plush in original packaging is the resale gold; loose plush is commodity
Tamagotchi: original 1996-98 era (P1/P2) commands premium; modern Tamagotchi Pix / Smart commodity
Furby: 1998-2000 original era + Furby Babies sub-line; identify via 'Tiger Electronics' stamping on belly tag
Pokemon TCG: 1st Edition stamp + holo + Base Set / Jungle / Fossil / Neo era = premium; modern sets commodity
Polly Pocket: pre-1998 'Bluebird' (UK manufacturer) era = premium $50-300; post-1998 Mattel reissue commodity $5-20
Cabbage Patch: 'Coleco' 1980s = premium $80-400; 'Hasbro' 1989-94 mid-tier; modern Play Along commodity
American Girl: 'Pleasant Company' 1986-2008 = premium ($100-600); modern Mattel-era 2008+ standard tier
Beanie Babies: 95%+ are commodity; specific errors / Princess Diana / Peace bear with PVC pellets / 1st gen tag = premium tier
Sealed / unopened / NRFB (Never Removed From Box) trades at 2-5x loose pricing

brands.notes: Webkinz UNUSED-CODE is the hidden-gem retail flip of nostalgia toys. Ganz launched the line 2005, peaked 2007-2010, declining ever since — supply is permanently fixed and codes are non-renewable so each unused code is genuinely scarce. The hangtag MUST be attached AND the foil scratch-off area MUST be intact. Cut-tag / used-code Webkinz are commodity-tier ~$5. Convention exclusives, Estore Exclusives, and retired-line variants (Cheeky / Bullfrog / Persian Cat) command 3-5x standard pricing.

brands.notes: Neopets has a passionate adult collector base (millennials nostalgic for the 2000s site). Limited Too retail-exclusive plush + McDonald's Happy Meal 2004-2006 promos are the dominant collector tier. Each plush originally shipped with an unused-virtual-pet code; codes still work on Neopets.com so SEALED packaging with code intact commands premium over loose plush.

brands.notes: Tiger Electronics Furby (1998-2000) is the foundational virtual-pet plush. Verify the 'Tiger Electronics' belly-tag stamping — modern Hasbro reissues (2012+ Furby Boom, 2023 Furby) are NOT vintage premium tier. Working IR sensors + eyes-blinking-and-talking adds 50%. brands.notes: Bluebird-era Polly Pocket (1989-1998 UK manufacturer) is the resale apex — Mattel acquired the brand in 1998 and changed the format from 'compact-with-mini-figures' to 'larger plastic dolls'. The pre-1998 Bluebird compacts are what millennials remember and what collectors pay premium for. Verify 'Bluebird' stamping on the case base. Disney crossover compacts (Beauty & Beast, Aladdin, Snow White) are the apex sub-tier. Missing figures kill value 50-70%.

brands.notes: WOTC-era Pokemon TCG (1999-2003) is the apex of TCG nostalgia collecting. 1st Edition stamp is the most important visual signal — sets the price tier. Sealed WOTC booster packs/boxes from this era trade $200-15K depending on set + condition. Graded (PSA/BGS/CGC) cards trade 3-10x ungraded. PriceCharting's classifier already routes these correctly to the curated catalog (free comp), but BOLO matching surfaces them in the picker for prioritization.

comp_ranges_usd.item: Princess Diana Beanie Baby PVC pellets MWMT

brands.notes: BEANIE BABIES ARE 95% COMMODITY. Standard ones trade $1-5. Tier-3 (low priority) deliberately — only specific names/errors/1st-gen-tags command real money. Princess Diana 1997 with PVC pellets and MWMT (mint-with-mint-tags) is the volume premium tier. Tag errors (e.g., 'Quackers' missing 'a') and 1st-gen-tag examples (no swing tag, 1993-94) are the apex but extremely rare. Most 'Beanie Baby collection' lots are $5 commodity boxes — verify specific names + tag condition before paying.

platform_notes.eBay: Dominant marketplace for nostalgia toys. Use sold-listings filter heavily — asking prices on Beanie/Webkinz/Polly Pocket are often 5-10x what they actually clear at.
platform_notes.Mercari: Strong for Webkinz, Neopets, Tamagotchi (lower fees + younger demographic familiar with the products).
platform_notes.TCGplayer: Standard comp benchmark for Pokemon / Yu-Gi-Oh card prices. Don't sell here for rare cards — eBay reaches more grading-tier buyers.
platform_notes.Etsy: Vintage 20+ years gets a 10-20% Etsy lift on Pleasant Company / Bluebird Polly Pocket / Coleco Cabbage Patch. Skip for modern reissues.
platform_notes.PSA / BGS / CGC: Grading services. Add 30-50% turnaround cost to a card's price but slabbed cards trade 2-10x raw. Worth it on $200+ cards.
